changes.title: Explicit self-update
changes.description: ohgo update installs the published release after verifying its SHA-256, and a failed verification restores the previous binary.

changes.title: Complete update lifecycle
changes.description: A successful /update now offers a one-shot What's New acknowledgement on the next interactive launch.

changes.title: Improved TUI update handling
changes.description: The update hint remains informational, installation stays explicit, and the restart requirement is named truthfully.

changes.title: Space jumps to the live edge
changes.description: In the full-screen transcript, `space` returns to the latest line when the composer is idle and the view is scrolled up. A non-empty draft keeps space literal.

changes.title: One-line install
changes.description: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PizenLabs/ohgo/main/install.sh | sh` resolves the latest stable release (or a pinned `OHGO_VERSION`), verifies the tarball against `sha256sums.txt`, smoke-tests the binary, and installs into `$HOME/.local/bin`. A mismatch leaves an existing installation untouched.

changes.title: `/copy` with `-a` and `-c` scopes
changes.description: The default copies the most valuable part of the latest answer without fences; `-a`/`--all` keeps the explanation and every code block, and `-c`/`--context` copies the conversation context. A terminal that cannot accept OSC 52 is reported rather than claiming success.

changes.title: Evidence benchmark suite
changes.description: `go run ./bench/phase9 -suite evidence` measures the five runtime requirement tasks and the authority regression matrix with the real router, security gate, evidence projector, and completion evaluator. It also runs against a live provider with `-live-model`.

changes.title: External-state claims need observation
changes.description: An answer that turns local configuration into a remote fact ("the workflow ran today", "it was pushed") is `NEEDS_REVIEW` unless the run observed the remote surface through a knowledge call, an MCP capability, or a command that talked to a remote.

changes.title: Evidence-aware stop
changes.description: After the first observation turn, a turn that observes the repository without adding a new fact stops informational work from starting another tool round. The decision derives from evidence gain, never from a tool-call count.

changes.title: Repository questions demand evidence
changes.description: Questions about this repository's behaviour ("does this workflow run automatically?") declare a `repository_overview` need that only a content-bearing observation satisfies; a listing or an answer from memory is `NEEDS_REVIEW`.

changes.title: Questions are not execution requests
changes.description: Authority admission no longer escalates an informational question that contains execution or mutation vocabulary, so "I want to ask if this automatically runs" classifies as READ and runs in ASK.

changes.title: "Investigate" routes to FUZZ
changes.description: "Investigate …", "diagnose …", and "troubleshoot …" now classify as INVESTIGATE (FUZZ) instead of falling back to READ.

changes.title: Hosting names are not code symbols
changes.description: Hosting and product names such as "GitHub" are no longer extracted as code symbol targets, so a request that mentions one no longer demands impossible index evidence.

changes.title: Task continuity Phase 1
changes.description: the durable task now owns structured, role-independent context (verified facts, hypotheses, evidence references, questions) and isolated ASK/FUZZ/BUILD execution contexts in `progress.json`. Context is assembled deterministically for the active role with existing character and token bounds; it survives restart, session continuation, and task resume, and it never grants authority. Model assertions remain hypotheses until current evidence confirms them, and contradictory evidence is retained without overwriting facts.

changes.title: Task continuity runtime population
changes.description: material tool observations are folded into task evidence references at the turn boundary, successful checks become evidence-backed facts, and ASK/FUZZ/BUILD role contexts carry their own observed progress. A role change on the same objective keeps the task and its contexts instead of detaching it. Semantic hypotheses, questions, reasoning, and strategy remain host writes because the runtime has no trustworthy signal for them.

changes.title: Task continuity Phase 2
changes.description: a widening role transition is now a controlled handoff. `workspace.ProposeHandoff` asks for the authority the request needs; the human approves through the existing in-chat transition decision; the existing `SwitchWorkspace` seam performs the only authority move. The task records a bounded handoff (roles, objective, truthfully measured workspace state, and references to the shared facts, hypotheses, questions, evidence, and artifacts) in `progress.json`. Applied handoffs keep one task identity and all role contexts in both directions; rejected, failed, and interrupted handoffs never change the recorded role. A restart reconciles an approved handoff against the authority that was actually restored: a matching target is recorded as applied without a second switch or a resumed turn, a matching source is reported as not applied, and any third role is reported as a recovery discrepancy without rewriting the recorded role. A transition's source is the live authority, so recovered stale task metadata cannot block a valid narrowing, and a checkpoint recovered without `task.md` reconstructs the objective from the contract so its handoff stays valid and writable.

changes.title: Task continuity Phase 3
changes.description: progression, lineage, recovery, and evidence-backed completion. `progress.json` now carries a bounded timeline of meaningful task events (creation, checkpoints, findings, evidence and hypothesis dispositions, handoffs, verification, detach/resume, completion, failure) that references authoritative records instead of copying payloads, plus an evidence proof for COMPLETED tasks. `Task.ObjectiveState` distinguishes `ACTIVE`, `INTERRUPTED`, `NEEDS_REVIEW`, `BLOCKED`, `PROVEN`, `COMPLETED_UNPROVEN`, and `CANCELLED`. Completion is explicit per contract kind: an informational objective needs an answer, an execution objective needs a projected successful execution (an answer alone is refused), and a mutation objective needs an observed change plus a verification that followed it. A proof that is invalidated, superseded, evicted, or materially contradicted downgrades to `COMPLETED_UNPROVEN` without rewriting the lifecycle record. Load reports whether recovery was intact, reconstructed with named missing information, in need of a human decision, or blocked; detached archives carry the same classification and corrupt archive files are reported instead of silently skipped. `/task status`, `/task show`, `/task timeline`, and `/task lineage` expose the same read-only facts through the existing interaction surface.

changes.title: `progress.json` is now schema version 3
changes.description: The bump is a downgrade barrier, not a shape change: a newer binary still reads version 1 and 2 checkpoints, while an older binary refuses version 3 instead of silently rewriting it without the timeline and completion proof it cannot parse. The projection is written before the checkpoint, and the checkpoint write is the commit point.

changes.title: The task timeline elides observation events before lifecycle history and counts dropped events from
changes.description: the retained sequence numbers rather than assuming the first retained event is the creation event. Repeated pause and review boundaries are idempotent, and task-context mutations use the injected clock.

changes.title: A failed completion checkpoint can no longer be published as `COMPLETED`/`PROVEN`: the controller
changes.description: restores the prior task and the TUI refuses to surface an uncommitted completion. The same task stays resumable.

changes.title: A successful command is projected as an observation, so an execution objective can be backed by
changes.description: real execution evidence rather than only by a final answer. The durable boundary also carries a check's reported scope and refuses a verification that does not cover the contract's declared kind and scope.

changes.title: Recovery no longer reports `INTACT` after dropping or repairing a completion proof, archive
changes.description: sanitization reports its repairs, and resuming an archive preserves that classification.

changes.title: A contradiction now downgrades `PROVEN` when it targets a claim the proof depends on, and leaves an
changes.description: unrelated proof intact.

changes.title: Task context selection now uses the fixed budget with relevance ordering instead of recency-only
changes.description: caps: older verified facts survive, the active role's section is reserved, stale evidence cannot displace current evidence, and an overfull section reports how many items it omitted.

changes.title: Task-context repair now deduplicates role contexts across the whole collection, clears dangling
changes.description: supersession pointers, rewrites invalidated confirmations, and refuses to hand back a context that would make every later checkpoint fail validation.

changes.title: A dedup key can no longer silently reuse an earlier record for a different observation, and a fact
changes.description: confirmed from a hypothesis records the confirming role while the hypothesis keeps the proposing role.

changes.title: A quit now cancels an in-flight background update check
changes.description: the observer is bound to the TUI program or plain-REPL lifetime, so leaving ohgo stops the request instead of leaving it running behind a surface that no longer exists.

changes.title: The background check and `/update` now share one update service
changes.description: discovery and installation read and write the same cache, so a hint and an explicit update cannot disagree about which release is current.

changes.title: A cancelled update check is no longer persisted
changes.description: quitting during a check no longer records a failed attempt that suppressed the next eligible check for a TTL.

changes.title: Provider tool-call normalization
changes.description: assistant text that carries a serialized `<invoke>` or `<tool_call>` envelope becomes a canonical tool call before the agent loop or transcript sees it. Every provider stream is normalized, native calls pass through unchanged, and malformed, incomplete, or oversized envelopes stay visible as ordinary text instead of being fabricated or silently dropped.

changes.title: Contextual task rail
changes.description: a responsive right-hand rail shows the active task, its open todos, active integrations, and task insights only while an execution request has open todos. Idle, question-only, and completed or cancelled tasks keep the full-width transcript; a sticky row keeps the task anchored when the rail does not fit, and every section is row-bounded for steady frame cost.

changes.title: `/settings` preferences
changes.description: the new preferences surface toggles the task rail in place and persists it as `taskRail` in `settings.json`, defaulting to enabled. It participates in the shared modal, keyboard, wheel, overlay, composer, and welcome ownership rules.

changes.title: Syntax-highlighted diffs
changes.description: approvals and expanded tool blocks render tinted additions and removals so a mutation can be reviewed without leaving the transcript.

changes.title: Live reasoning and activity
changes.description: throttled Braille spinners mark responding and live-reasoning phases, and one live activity row carries a measured duration plus streaming tool output.

changes.title: Transcript presentation
changes.description: tool runs stay contiguous across streamed text, markdown paragraph breaks survive, reasoning collapses behind a toggle, paths and URLs middle-truncate, and filesystem errors reduce to one-line summaries. Reasoning and tool identity survive session resume, and the recap footer comes from observed evidence and the answer's finding rather than the tool list.

changes.title: Evidence and grounding
changes.description: pruned, truncated, or timed-out scans are incomplete evidence rather than proof of absence; glob output names gitignore-skipped paths, passive search failures are detected, and implementation language is derived from nested manifests the run actually read.

changes.title: Task closure and final answers
changes.description: an answer-only surface withdraws every tool, unproductive turns are bounded, and a failure ledger with provenance attribution keeps the final answer truthful. A blocked task is reported as review rather than success.

changes.title: Provider stream ordering
changes.description: OpenAI and Ollama keep text emitted after a native tool call in its logical position instead of merging it into the trailing block.

changes.title: Closed-surface answers
changes.description: post-answer tool calls are dropped instead of appearing as refusal cards, while policy refusals remain visible in the transcript and session.

changes.title: Informational completion
changes.description: deferred-plan narration ("I will …") no longer completes an informational objective; the run needs an answer.

changes.title: File-count claims
changes.description: exclusive counts are checked against the files the run actually observed.

changes.title: Tool-call leakage
changes.description: serialized calls inside assistant prose no longer leak into visible content or bypass execution; diagnostics name malformed or incomplete envelopes rather than guessing.

changes.title: Session concurrency
changes.description: session startup and sequence allocation are hardened for concurrent writers.

changes.title: Hybrid master-prompt offloading
changes.description: prompts with at least 50 lines or 4000 runes are written to `<project>/.ohgo/scratch/prompt_<session>_<timestamp>.md` and their bytes are injected directly into the model payload. A durable history copy is written first, so Up/Down and Ctrl+P/N still recall the full prompt after scratch is removed. Scratch is cleaned on session close/switch, on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP, and by a 24-hour startup sweep.

changes.title: Session protection
changes.description: `t` in the Session Manager toggles a durable `Protected` tag, shown as a star in the status column and as `Protected · yes/no` in the details pane. Tagged sessions are never removed by automatic pruning while explicit deletion still works.

changes.title: Retention controls
changes.description: `/settings` gains a CLEANUP section with auto-prune, keep-recent count, and a manual-clean action. The new `ohgo clean` command performs the same protected-aware pruning from the shell.

changes.title: Deterministic prompt optimization
changes.description: `internal/promptopt` compresses oversized scratch prompts and sanitizes local session titles without a model call or a third-party dependency. Compression removes greetings, politeness, and markdown decoration while preserving fenced code, inline code, paths, and identifiers; local titles drop conversational noise, respect hard word/rune bounds at word boundaries, and never end on a dangling article or preposition.

changes.title: Local-first session titling
changes.description: every session title is derived synchronously from the submitted prompt by `promptopt.SanitizeTitle` before any provider request. The background ASK-model titler, its timeout and backfill workers, and the "generating title…" placeholder are removed. Legacy untitled sessions are labeled locally when the Session Manager opens, so titles appear instantly with zero token cost.

changes.title: Adaptive execution experience
changes.description: `internal/experience` extracts deterministic incidents from completed turns, derives bounded lessons and candidate path preferences, and applies only promoted experience. The projector may reorder already-offered tools and append bounded advisory hints; authority, evidence, completion, budgets, and task state are unchanged. `/experience` inspects or retires records, and `<project>/.ohgo/experience.json` is a versioned, bounded, cold-start-safe store.

changes.title: Transcript markdown fences and wrapping
changes.description: an indented fence under a list item stays a code block, wrapped bullet continuations are joined before wrapping, and an ordered marker is budgeted by its real width. A long continuation previously bypassed the wrap pass, reached the terminal as one oversized row, and was truncated at the right edge; nested examples also printed their fence delimiters literally instead of rendering as code.

changes.title: Automatic appearance
changes.description: `internal/tui/design` is now the single token source for a Dark and a Light palette, and `theme` is stored as a preference — `auto`, `dark`, or `light` — resolved once at startup. `auto` follows the host appearance on macOS, Linux, and Windows behind a bounded poll with a dark fallback, so a light terminal is legible without per-view overrides. `/theme` switches the appearance in place.

changes.title: Inline composer hints
changes.description: the binding suggestion is painted at the input origin ahead of the caret while the composer is empty, so the prompt reads as embedded instead of displaced. Hints are grouped by interaction (onboarding, ASK, BUILD, FUZZ) and advance within the active group on submit and on authority change; the first keystroke replaces the hint without touching the buffer. The quickstart command grid and its per-project random tip are removed in favour of one framed panel with a static tip.

changes.title: Split-pane task visibility
changes.description: on narrow and medium terminals the task area is now pinned below the title bar for the whole open task instead of collapsing to a single row and releasing when the last todo is marked done. It renders the bounded projection block and a spacer, so scrolling moves only the transcript below it. The rail now closes on the terminal task transition, matching the wide sidebar, rather than on the last completed todo.

changes.title: Interrupted BUILD continuation
changes.description: a resumed task now derives its execution stage from durable evidence, so a change applied before the interruption stays in post-change verification. The task briefing carries a resume directive naming the last observed change, the pending check, and the rule against re-planning or repeating completed discovery.

changes.title: Runaway continuation
changes.description: the control plane now stops a run after `MaxConsecutiveNoProgress` completed turns that do not change the task boundary. During verification only a change or a check counts; elsewhere new evidence, a stage/requirement change, or an explicit blocker counts. The stop is reported as `NEEDS_REVIEW` with its semantic reason, not as a model-turn limit. The model-turn cap remains the last-resort resource bound.

changes.title: BUILD implementation continuity
changes.description: after a change is applied but not yet verified, a refinement prompt such as “I want to use green and black” now inherits the open mutation contract instead of being rebuilt as a new informational task. The task identity, change evidence, and write surface continue under BUILD, and the refinement still owes the same post-change verification. Explicit mutation prompts keep BUILD and the write surface as new objectives. Read questions, investigation requests, and explicit no-mutation limits remain new objectives; a no-mutation request that also asks to understand offers the ASK boundary.

changes.title: Rework follow-ups
changes.description: `redesign`, `rework`, `revamp`, `restyle`, `redo`, `overhaul`, `modernize`, `redraw`, `reimplement`, and `rearchitect` are repository-change heads. After a design turn, “redesign it” now derives a mutation contract in BUILD, offers the write surface, and cannot be proven from another plan or a recorded change artifact without an observed change and a later check.

changes.title: Task plan isolation
changes.description: a new task starts with an empty session todo plan. The previous task keeps its todo snapshot in its archive, but its completed items no longer appear as the new task's progress or get imported into its checkpoint.

changes.title: Resumed investigation tasks
changes.description: repeating a task's own objective no longer bypasses workspace prediction. A BUILD task handed back with a strong investigation request now moves to FUZZ instead of staying in BUILD until a new session is started.

changes.title: FUZZ scratch execution
changes.description: a shell redirect to an absolute path outside the workspace is execution, not a repository mutation. Starting a local server that logs to a temporary file is no longer refused by semantic admission.

changes.title: Refused-proposal recovery
changes.description: a model that stops with no visible text immediately after a refusal-only turn now gets one answer-only request from the evidence already gathered, rather than ending the task with an empty final message.

changes.title: Answer-only silence
changes.description: when the already-closed answer surface returns only reasoning, the loop makes one bounded answer-only retry, with a runtime-authored request that no tool is available, instead of ending the run with an empty final assistant message after a completed investigation.

changes.title: Investigation evidence retention
changes.description: trimming the durable evidence state now evicts transient command diagnostics before content-bearing file reads and directory listings. A long FUZZ run no longer loses the observations that satisfy `repository_overview` and `repository_survey`, which previously kept the answer boundary closed and the investigation reported as insufficient.

changes.title: LongCat serialized tool calls
changes.description: `<longcat_tool_call>` envelopes in assistant text are now normalized at the provider boundary in both the JSON and key/value spellings. Previously the raw protocol reached the transcript as prose and the proposed calls were never authorized or executed.

changes.title: Composer footer hierarchy
changes.description: while a turn runs, the measured timer and session telemetry now hold the left edge and the queue/cancel/scroll keys pin to the right edge in the faint tier. Joined into one sentence, the keys trailed the metrics and read as more telemetry, so the footer competed with the transcript and left the right half of the row empty.

changes.title: Intelligent context compaction
changes.description: The loop now measures the *projected* next request (messages, system blocks, tool definitions, durable task projection, expected output, safety margin) and classifies pressure as `NORMAL`/`MONITOR`/`PREPARE`/`COMPACT`/`CRITICAL`. `agent.CompactWith` applies deterministic deduplication and size bounds first, then rebuilds from the control plane's authoritative `ContextProjection` (authority, objective, completion, durable orientation blocks) plus a bounded recent suffix, and only falls back to a semantic summary when no valid projection exists. Replaced tool output is archived under stable ids and retrievable with the new read-only `recall` tool. Rewrites are bounded per run and a request that still cannot fit returns `ErrContextOverflow` instead of sending it or claiming completion. `/compact` runs the same pipeline manually with one activity-line lifecycle; its terminal result reports measured before/after estimated tokens and only the state/evidence categories the structured outcome preserved, with a degraded label when the semantic fallback ran.

changes.title: Unified investigation orchestration
changes.description: `intelligence/investigate` executes the planner's plan as a closed loop (`PLAN → EXECUTE ONE STEP → OBSERVE → CORRELATE → REASSESS`). One shared evidence engine receives every provider's records, one meter bounds LSP/DAP requests, and each run reports selected and skipped providers with reasons, observed confidence/coverage, contradictions, and the stop reason. Provider adapters cover structural analysis, the shared Okapi BM25F workspace, live LSP declarations/references/call hierarchy, and an already-authorized stopped debug session. `planner.Reassess` never re-selects an executed provider and only reports "no provider" when the target is genuinely unmet. The new `investigate` tool is the model-facing entrypoint and returns bounded facts instead of raw payloads. Composition shares one retrieval workspace between `retrieve` and `investigate`, and starts `gopls` lazily when installed. `bench/intelligence` measures retrieval cold/warm/query cost and adaptive provider selection at 100–50,000 synthetic files.

changes.title: The live telemetry bar now names the concrete action instead of a fixed phase
changes.description: A running tool's argument payload maps deterministically to a present-participle description (`reading retry.go`, `running tests`, `resolving dependencies`); an open thought channel contributes its primary action (`inspecting the repository`). Phrases are lowercase and carry no trailing dots, while paths and code symbols keep their spelling. Phrases hold a 500ms display floor and coalesce bursts to the newest still-live action, so fast calls cannot flicker the row. The shimmer is now a 30 FPS `float64` wave with a radius-5 cosine falloff, bold intensity above 0.65, and TrueColor interpolation between the muted and primary text roles; terminals without TrueColor keep the plain styled phrase.

changes.title: `structure` separates the facts that fail independently
changes.description: `scope_gaps` names the excluded source files instead of reporting only a count, and a view whose structural coverage is incomplete states `source_access: AVAILABLE`, so missing adapter coverage is never read as a denied read. A project whose extensions have no registry entry at all is classified `UNSUPPORTED` instead of `PARTIAL`, which had invited waiting for parsing that can never happen.

changes.title: A review that rejects an absence claim now names the observation that refutes it
changes.description: `ls` and `glob` publish the paths they observed, and the claim audit reports "the answer says X is absent, but this run observed app/X.tsx" instead of "X is absent without evidence covering the claim". The audit also reports the specific subject ("portfolio file") rather than the bare noun a pattern matched ("file").

changes.title: A tool the control plane judged unable to close the current gap (an inventory listing when the
changes.description: answer still needs component source) is now reported in the runtime briefing instead of withdrawn from the request. The withdrawal rewrote the tool block, and a provider cache matches a prefix, so it invalidated every cached token behind the block: an observed broad-analysis session dropped from 13,920 reused bytes to 527 on the request that changed the tools. The action surface now changes only for capability and authority verdicts.

changes.title: An unenumerable workspace root is now one environment blocker instead of a run of unrelated tool
changes.description: failures. `cognition.ProbeFacts` records the root enumeration error (`RepositoryFacts.RootError`) while keeping the markers it could still stat, the runtime block leads with the restriction, and the projection closes the task with the measured cause when the objective needs a listing. `glob` no longer answers `No files matched` for a directory it never read: the scan error is returned as `execution_failed`, and `ls` classifies an unreadable directory the same way instead of reporting a remote tool error. Previously a permission-denied root cost four turns and ended on "no meaningful task progress", naming neither the path nor the cause.

changes.title: Context construction now protects the provider's prompt cache
changes.description: Every request has three regions in order: the stable system prefix and tool definitions, the append-only conversation, and one trailing `ai.RuntimeStateMessage`. Per-turn state — referenced files, the task continuity briefing, a standing proposal decision, the projection's runtime state block, and one-shot recovery directives — travels in that suffix instead of a system block, so the bytes before it stay identical between turns. `Loop.freezePrefix` restores the form an already-sent message was first sent with, and the projector bounds each tool result by its own size rather than by a moving "recent results" window, which used to rewrite cached history on every request. Compaction remains the only deliberate prefix break and reports itself as an expected rewind. `agent.UsageLog` records one `CacheSample` per request; `ClassifyCache` separates an `EXPECTED` drop (system, tools, model, or rewind changed) from a `SUSPICIOUS` one (the prefix repeated and less was reused), and `/usage` renders the ratio, the uncached input, and the verdict. The Anthropic transport marks the final system block and the last stable conversation turn as cache breakpoints. Measured on the production provider path, cached input over a ten-request session rose from 4,992 to 14,824 tokens with no per-request regression.

changes.title: Compaction settings now include `keepRecentToolResults`, `expectedOutputTokens`,
changes.description: `safetyMarginPercent`, `monitorPercent`, `preparePercent`, and `maxAttempts`. State-first reconstruction never updates or replaces durable task state, so authority, objective, facts, hypotheses, verification results, and completion survive compaction unchanged.

changes.title: Retrieval postings now reference integer document slots instead of path strings: query-only p50 at
changes.description: 20,000 documents fell from 23 ms to 5 ms, and the per-posting string header and map lookup are gone. The AST inventory exposes the observed modification time, so retrieval no longer stats every file a second time after the inventory's freshness pass (refresh 243 ms → 183 ms).

changes.title: The DAP dial-client transport is validated with a real subprocess over loopback and composed into
changes.description: the investigation orchestrator: runtime records land in the shared evidence engine and consume the shared DAP meter.

changes.title: Real debugger validation
changes.description: `TestRealDlvRuntimeEvidence` now passes against `dlv dap` when macOS developer mode is enabled. The fixture is built with `-gcflags=all=-N -l` and canonical paths so the known breakpoint verifies; the session stops, exposes threads/stack/scopes/variables through the runtime provider, continues to exit, and closes as `TERMINATED`.

changes.title: `bench/intelligence` reports median/p95 over repeated rounds and can measure memory per phase in a
changes.description: fresh process (`-phase ast|retrieval|investigation`). The 5k refresh "regression" was variance: median 48 ms, p95 52 ms. Memory at 20k files decomposes to 94.5 MiB AST snapshot, +43.3 MiB retrieval index, +0.1 MiB investigation state.

changes.title: Runtime DAP transport
changes.description: added the dial-client mode Delve requires (`dlv dap --client-addr={addr}`). The launch request is sent without blocking, so adapters that answer launch only after `configurationDone` no longer deadlock the handshake. A real fixture reaches initialize + launch; the integration test skips on machines where developer mode is disabled and debugserver cannot run the debuggee.

changes.title: Retrieval benchmark
changes.description: query-only cost is now measured separately from reconciliation (23 ms vs 225 ms at 20,000 documents). No BM25F change was made because the profile did not justify one.

changes.title: Retrieval warm load
changes.description: persisted documents are decoded from a columnar envelope and posting lists are sorted once per load instead of once per document. Measured on the synthetic benchmark: 20,000 documents 12.3 s → 353 ms; 50,000 files 13.4 s → 554 ms. The old per-document sort was quadratic in the number of documents sharing a term.

changes.title: Adaptive structural intelligence
changes.description: `intelligence/structural` interprets the shared `ast.Index` snapshot as a typed, multi-resolution model instead of a flat inventory. It owns evidence states (`OBSERVED`, `PARTIALLY_OBSERVED`, `INFERRED`, `VERIFIED`, `UNKNOWN`) with weakest-link confidence, source-class classification, a strategy portfolio, an intent-aware planner with recorded cost/reason/stopping decisions, bounded graph intelligence (SCC, cycles, condensation, layering, degree and bounded betweenness centrality), a bounded modularity strategy (`modularity-label-propagation`), and a versioned analysis cache keyed by schema, analyzer, snapshot identity, and request. `structure` adds `analysis` and `expand` views plus `intent`, `level`, and `node` arguments; the engine is read-only and reuses the existing snapshot, impact resolver, and authorization boundaries. `ast` adds whole-snapshot `Inventory` and language-neutral `Dependencies` projections for in-process analysis. Canonical documentation: [`docs/architecture/STRUCTURAL_INTELLIGENCE.md`](docs/architecture/STRUCTURAL_INTELLIGENCE.md).

changes.title: Semantic intelligence
changes.description: `intelligence/semantic` implements the LSP JSON-RPC client and a lazy, deduplicated, bounded server manager: capability negotiation, document synchronization, definition/references/document and workspace symbols, hover, call hierarchy, and diagnostics, with per-request timeout, cancellation, crash surfacing, and restart bounds. It never applies workspace edits: `workspace/applyEdit`, rename, and execute-command paths are refused so BUILD remains the only mutation authority. Verified against a fake protocol server and real `gopls`.

changes.title: Runtime intelligence
changes.description: `intelligence/runtime` implements the Debug Adapter Protocol client and an authorized session manager with explicit states (`CREATED` … `TERMINATED`/`FAILED`), bounded sessions, breakpoints, threads, stack traces, scopes, variables, stepping, exceptions, and gated `evaluate`. Launch/attach/evaluate/terminate require an injected authorizer; cleanup disconnects, then kills the adapter process group so a hung adapter cannot orphan the debuggee. Reverse requests are refused.

changes.title: Retrieval
changes.description: `intelligence/retrieval` implements Okapi BM25F over path, identifier, and comment fields with language-aware tokenization, exact identifier and path reranking, bounded postings, deterministic ranking, incremental per-file updates, deletion, and a versioned persisted index. `retrieve` exposes bounded ranked candidates to the model. A labeled corpus test measures MRR/Recall@5 against a path-search baseline; `bench/retrieval` reports cold/warm/refresh cost and query latency on a real repository.

changes.title: Unified evidence
changes.description: `intelligence/evidence` owns the shared state vocabulary (structural now aliases it), content-addressed records with provider/source/ scope/freshness provenance, deduplication, agreement grouping, and preserved contradictions. `VERIFIED` requires an explicit proof constructor, so a successful provider call cannot upgrade an observation.

changes.title: Intelligence planner
changes.description: `intelligence/planner` selects a bounded, deterministic provider plan per intent with cost bands, expected confidence, stopping reasons, and explicit skip reasons (including "no authorized runtime session"). It is a pure decision layer: it starts no process and grants no authority.

changes.title: Shared wire framing
changes.description: `intelligence/wire` owns the Content-Length JSON transport used by both LSP and DAP, with one size bound and one malformed frame contract.

changes.title: Structured verification runtime
changes.description: the `verify` capability owns a service lifecycle (`STARTING`/`RUNNING`/`READY`/`FAILED`/`STOPPING`/`STOPPED`/ `TIMED_OUT`), HTTP/TCP/output readiness, port discovery, bounded HTTP and command checks, an optional headless-browser check, and process-group cleanup on every exit path. Independent checks run with bounded concurrency; browser verification is optional and reports `VERIFICATION_INSUFFICIENT` when no headless browser exists.

changes.title: Structured normalization evidence
changes.description: provider envelopes that fail to parse now carry `ToolNormalizationFailure` records (`INCOMPLETE`, `INVALID`, `UNSUPPORTED`) with a bounded raw fragment, protocol, provider, and recoverability. The raw fragment is audit-only and is never executed or published as an answer.

changes.title: Project structural runtime
changes.description: `ast.Index` is now an incremental snapshot over files, packages, configs, tests, and entrypoints, with `CURRENT`/`UPDATING`/ `STALE`/`INVALID` freshness, generation, snapshot identity, parse-failure disclosure, and a bounded `structure` read-only tool. Incremental refresh parses only changed Go files and re-resolves relationships from retained raw syntax. `graph`, `refs`, and `structure` now enter `cognition` as structural evidence carrying snapshot provenance and completeness.

changes.title: Adaptive multi-language structural runtime
changes.description: Go keeps its native backend; pinned tree-sitter adapters add TypeScript/TSX, JavaScript/JSX, Java, C#, Rust, Kotlin, Ruby, C, and C++ over the same `ast.Index`. Canonical facts preserve language-specific kinds, visibility, containers, imports, explicit inheritance/implementation clauses, calls, tests, entries, and source coordinates. `structure` adds `languages` and `relations` views; `symbols` and `refs` expose language/native-kind/exported provenance. A no-cgo build keeps Go and reports the other extensions as unsupported.

changes.title: Adaptive activation
changes.description: `TaskShape` derives `NONE`/`OVERVIEW`/`TARGETED`/ `IMPACT` from existing shape signals, withholds structural tools at `NONE`, and lets overviews stay metadata-first. Targeted/impact queries parse pending supported files on demand; semantic escalation is explicitly unsupported.

changes.title: Structural evidence now carries language, adapter, resolution, structural completeness,
changes.description: project-scope completeness, and truncation in addition to snapshot id and generation (`EvidenceVersion` 4). Snapshots disclose per-language parsed/pending/failed counts, inventory completeness, structural completeness, and unsupported source extensions.

changes.title: Project-boundary scope
changes.description: a nested repository is included in the same structural snapshot even when the enclosing repository's `.gitignore` hides its directory, and the nested repository's own ignore rules govern its contents. `structure` adds a metadata-only `scope` view, and snapshots report `nested_projects`, `excluded_roots`, file-level `excluded_source_files`, the decisive rule, shallow build markers, `test_files`, and independent scope/inventory/structural/result completeness.

changes.title: Evidence claim classes
changes.description: `cognition` now classifies each observation as documentation, configuration/manifest, implementation source, or runtime, and retains bounded structural counts such as `test_files` (`EvidenceVersion` 5). The pre-answer runtime state block reports which classes the run supports, so the model sees the claim boundary before it writes instead of learning it only from a completion review.

changes.title: Evidence-to-claim completion
changes.description: provenance now distinguishes documentation, configuration/manifest, inventory, source path, source content, source import, source use, structural evidence, and runtime (`EvidenceVersion` 6); the state block derives an actionable evidence frontier and dependency strength. Component identity is path-derived and shared with the answer audit, so source from one component cannot support another. Strong completeness claims require an observed component source scope; dependency wording follows the `DECLARED`/`IMPORTED`/`INITIALIZED`/`USED_IN_SOURCE`/ `OBSERVED_AT_RUNTIME` ladder; unbounded concept absences stay review; and an identical read-only observation in a later turn is reused instead of re-executed.

changes.title: Source-citation audit
changes.description: an answer that presents a repository file as evidence (`(lib/search.ts)`) must have opened it. A listing proves the path exists, not what it does, so a citation of an unread file is now a review (`unsupported_source_citation`) instead of an inspected-looking inference. Prose mentions, route tables, and non-source files are not citations.

changes.title: Dependency-wiring audit
changes.description: a mechanism phrase attached to a declared dependency ("FlexSearch with a build-time prebuilt index") is now a review (`unsupported_wiring_claim`) unless source evidence of that dependency was observed. Dependency names are read from the manifests the run actually opened, not from a hardcoded ecosystem list; a version-only stack row, and a property in the next comma-separated item, stay declaration claims.

changes.title: An observation reused from an earlier turn now replays the recorded payload instead of a first-line
changes.description: summary. The previous notice named the coordinate and withheld the evidence, so the model had to repeat the call to recover data it had already paid for; the replay is bounded at 32 KiB and states the cut.

changes.title: `structure` has one entrypoint authority
changes.description: The overview and the `entrypoints` view derive from the same merged list and report `verified`/`discovered` totals, so a convention-discovered route module (`app/page.tsx`) can no longer be counted in one view and missing from the other. A framework route module stays a discovery even after parsing: the adapter matched its path, which is not proof that it executes.

changes.title: The structure header names what each axis covers (`scope
changes.description: COMPLETE (path inclusion)`, `inventory: COMPLETE (file observation)`, and `graph_state` qualified by whether structural knowledge is complete). A snapshot whose source has no adapter can no longer read as a complete understanding of the repository.

changes.title: `ls` accepts `depth` and walks a bounded pre-order tree in one read-only call, honouring
changes.description: `.gitignore` and pruning dependency/build directories, with an explicit notice when the entry limit stopped the walk. This is the topology primitive a read-only session needs without shell access.

changes.title: Repository scoping is injected into the structural index from the shared `ignore.Matcher`, so
changes.description: `.gitignore` membership has one owner and `ast` stays a dependency-free intelligence leaf. A rule or scope fingerprint change refreshes membership without re-parsing unchanged source files. Structural scope treats a nested repository as a project boundary and evaluates that repository's own ignore rules inside it.

changes.title: `structure` overview no longer repeats `parsed_files`, `unsupported_source`, or the module line in
changes.description: both the header and the body. A repeated overview of the same snapshot is marked `repeated: true` so the model can recognize that it adds no new inventory facts.

changes.title: The completion recap now names what carried the answer instead of what the run opened first
changes.description: Inspected files are ranked by whether the answer cites them, then by returned content, so a survey that read README and settings before the source that answered the question no longer cites only the README. When more files were read than the footer names, it reports the total ("Inspected 5 files, including app/portfolio.tsx and README.md"), and a read that returned a window states its range ("truncated at 400 of 512 lines") instead of implying a whole-file reading.

changes.title: `graph` remains the Go package import graph; a non-Go selector is pointed at `structure`/`refs`
changes.description: instead of being folded into a false package edge. The structural snapshot remains in memory. `<project>/.ohgo/graph.db` is still reserved and unimplemented; no derived persistence was added.

changes.title: Configuration and manifest observations are no longer implementation evidence
changes.description: A Makefile, Compose file, dependency manifest, README, directory listing, or structural inventory declares topology, dependencies, or metadata; a broad project survey now requires an observed source read before it can close. The state block names that missing class directly.

changes.title: Unified investigation orchestration
changes.description: `intelligence/investigate` executes the planner's plan as a closed loop (`PLAN → EXECUTE ONE STEP → OBSERVE → CORRELATE → REASSESS`). One shared evidence engine receives every provider's records, one meter bounds LSP/DAP requests, and each run reports selected and skipped providers with reasons, observed confidence/coverage, contradictions, and the stop reason. Provider adapters cover structural analysis, the shared Okapi BM25F workspace, live LSP declarations/references/call hierarchy, and an already-authorized stopped debug session. `planner.Reassess` never re-selects an executed provider and only reports "no provider" when the target is genuinely unmet. The new `investigate` tool is the model-facing entrypoint and returns bounded facts instead of raw payloads. Composition shares one retrieval workspace between `retrieve` and `investigate`, and starts `gopls` lazily when installed. `bench/intelligence` measures retrieval cold/warm/query cost and adaptive provider selection at 100–50,000 synthetic files.

changes.title: Retrieval postings now reference integer document slots instead of path strings: query-only p50 at
changes.description: 20,000 documents fell from 23 ms to 5 ms, and the per-posting string header and map lookup are gone. The AST inventory exposes the observed modification time, so retrieval no longer stats every file a second time after the inventory's freshness pass (refresh 243 ms → 183 ms).

changes.title: The DAP dial-client transport is validated with a real subprocess over loopback and composed into
changes.description: the investigation orchestrator: runtime records land in the shared evidence engine and consume the shared DAP meter.

changes.title: Real debugger validation
changes.description: `TestRealDlvRuntimeEvidence` now passes against `dlv dap` when macOS developer mode is enabled. The fixture is built with `-gcflags=all=-N -l` and canonical paths so the known breakpoint verifies; the session stops, exposes threads/stack/scopes/variables through the runtime provider, continues to exit, and closes as `TERMINATED`.

changes.title: `bench/intelligence` reports median/p95 over repeated rounds and can measure memory per phase in a
changes.description: fresh process (`-phase ast|retrieval|investigation`). The 5k refresh "regression" was variance: median 48 ms, p95 52 ms. Memory at 20k files decomposes to 94.5 MiB AST snapshot, +43.3 MiB retrieval index, +0.1 MiB investigation state.

changes.title: Runtime DAP transport
changes.description: added the dial-client mode Delve requires (`dlv dap --client-addr={addr}`). The launch request is sent without blocking, so adapters that answer launch only after `configurationDone` no longer deadlock the handshake. A real fixture reaches initialize + launch; the integration test skips on machines where developer mode is disabled and debugserver cannot run the debuggee.

changes.title: Retrieval benchmark
changes.description: query-only cost is now measured separately from reconciliation (23 ms vs 225 ms at 20,000 documents). No BM25F change was made because the profile did not justify one.

changes.title: Retrieval warm load
changes.description: persisted documents are decoded from a columnar envelope and posting lists are sorted once per load instead of once per document. Measured on the synthetic benchmark: 20,000 documents 12.3 s → 353 ms; 50,000 files 13.4 s → 554 ms. The old per-document sort was quadratic in the number of documents sharing a term.

changes.title: Capability preflight
changes.description: `contract.IntentContract.RequiredCapabilities` derives the operations an objective needs (reading, the mutation operation the request names, command execution when the contract requires a check) and `workspace.PreflightTurn` compares them against the constructed tool set and the live authority before the first model turn. A missing mandatory capability is refused with zero provider requests, no tool call, and a task recorded as BLOCKED with the class `CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE`; it is not a model failure, a verification failure, or a review. `cognition.CapabilityGap` enforces the same invariant on every later request through `agent.ProjectionReport.MissingCapabilities`, and the loop returns `agent.ErrCapabilityUnavailable` before it sends the request. Reading is required but not blocking: an observation-free answer is still the evidence layer's review verdict.

changes.title: `RunVerdict.String()` names the run classification (`COMPLETED`, `NEEDS_REVIEW`, `PAUSED`,
changes.description: `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, `CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE`) so the TUI, the headless verdict, and durable task records share one vocabulary.

changes.title: Retrieval postings now reference integer document slots instead of path strings: query-only p50 at
changes.description: 20,000 documents fell from 23 ms to 5 ms, and the per-posting string header and map lookup are gone. The AST inventory exposes the observed modification time, so retrieval no longer stats every file a second time after the inventory's freshness pass (refresh 243 ms → 183 ms).

changes.title: The DAP dial-client transport is validated with a real subprocess over loopback and composed into
changes.description: the investigation orchestrator: runtime records land in the shared evidence engine and consume the shared DAP meter.

changes.title: Real debugger validation
changes.description: `TestRealDlvRuntimeEvidence` now passes against `dlv dap` when macOS developer mode is enabled. The fixture is built with `-gcflags=all=-N -l` and canonical paths so the known breakpoint verifies; the session stops, exposes threads/stack/scopes/variables through the runtime provider, continues to exit, and closes as `TERMINATED`.

changes.title: `bench/intelligence` reports median/p95 over repeated rounds and can measure memory per phase in a
changes.description: fresh process (`-phase ast|retrieval|investigation`). The 5k refresh "regression" was variance: median 48 ms, p95 52 ms. Memory at 20k files decomposes to 94.5 MiB AST snapshot, +43.3 MiB retrieval index, +0.1 MiB investigation state.

changes.title: A negated status is not a completion claim
changes.description: "Not production-ready" and "the frontend is not feature-complete" were audited as if the answer asserted the opposite; a negation that binds to the status word now exempts the sentence, while "production-ready service" remains a claim.

changes.title: An adjective-first status names its subject after the marker
changes.description: "Feature-complete UI with mock data" was reviewed as an unnamed component even though the sentence names the UI; the post-marker noun is read when no subject precedes the status.

changes.title: "Stubs
changes.description: api-gateway, cart-service, …" is a status list like "Stubs (health-check only): …". Every named service is a subject, so the ones the run never read are reviewed.

changes.title: A root-file absence is covered by a root listing
changes.description: "no LICENSE file" (and "no README file") is a concrete claim about the repository root, but the claim subject kept its trailing "file", so the root-file vocabulary did not recognize it and a true absence was reviewed.

changes.title: A claim's scope is its own sentence
changes.description: Session 324's "no LICENSE file" was promoted to a repository-wide claim by the word "repo" in the *next* sentence, and a parenthetical aside ("nested backend/.git (root repo ignores backend/)") was read as a scope marker. The scope window is now the claim's sentence with parentheticals removed, so neighbouring prose cannot widen a local claim.

changes.title: A dependency review quotes whole words
changes.description: Session 322's review read "T API under /api/v1, …" because the 40-byte window around the mention started inside "REST"; the quote now widens to word boundaries, so it reads "REST API under /api/v1, …".

changes.title: A colon list of components followed by an em-dash explanation is still a list
changes.description: "Stubs (health-check only): api-gateway, cart-service, delivery-service, notification-service — plain net/http /health + /ready" now names every service, so the three the run never read are reviewed instead of being dropped with the explanation's clause. The status label in the review also no longer ends in the opening parenthesis ("Stubs", not "Stubs (").

changes.title: A leading absence item introduces a concept list
changes.description: "No JWT, RabbitMQ client code, gRPC server, or migrations" is now a concept-absence conclusion; a bare "no X" elsewhere in a sentence ("no Cache-Control", "no database") stays an inventory fact the bounded survey admits.

changes.title: A description of the project is not a component list
changes.description: "go-ecommerce is a full-stack e-commerce platform, currently a work-in-progress scaffold" named `go-ecommerce`, `full-stack`, and `e-commerce` as review subjects — three coordinates no source path can satisfy. A status claim's subject now ends at the predicate's copula, a hyphenated token must have a component role (`product-service`, `api-gateway`; not a project name or a domain adjective), a route (`/admin`) is not a component, and every item of a colon list must be a component name rather than prose that happens to end in one.

changes.title: "Frontend auth is mock only (demo accounts
changes.description: admin@ecommerce.com)" named `auth` or the email address as the review subject although a file under `src/` derives to the frontend. A surface noun (`frontend`, `backend`, `client`, `web`, `ui`, `storefront`) now owns the feature phrase it qualifies, and a colon inside a parenthetical no longer starts a component list.

changes.title: An implementation claim's plain verb form is now audited
changes.description: "order-service also implements a checkout API (server-computed totals, idempotent order creation)" names a component and a capability; the capability list is read from the parenthetical as well as from a "with …" clause, and each named capability must appear in the observed source for that component. Reading only `cmd/order-service/main.go` no longer supports "idempotent order creation".

changes.title: "Auth is mock" is a status claim even without a completion adjective or a "mock data" noun
changes.description: The mock vocabulary now includes the copula form, so the observed source must show a mock marker instead of only the component path.

changes.title: A list-item absence about an implementation mechanism is now a concept-absence conclusion: "No real
changes.description: JWT/auth", "no RabbitMQ client code", "no gRPC server wired up". A bare "no Cache-Control" or "no database" is an inventory fact a bounded survey demonstrated and remains admissible.

changes.title: A dependency-strength review says what the run did observe ("only a declaration", "only an
changes.description: initialized client", "no declaration, import, initialization, or source use") instead of printing the internal `NOT_OBSERVED` label.

changes.title: A status word's subject is read from the text before it
changes.description: A colon after a status word introduces either a component list ("Fully implemented: product-service, order-service") or an explanation of the status ("It is an in-progress scaffold: the order-service now implements checkout, …"). Only the list form names subjects, so the explanation's verbs and adjectives are no longer reported as components ("checkout", "in-progress") in a review that no source path can satisfy.

changes.title: A test-absence review now names the contradiction it already holds
changes.description: when an observed structure snapshot reported test files, "No Go tests exist" is answered with that count ("the observed inventory already reports 5 test file(s)") instead of asking for evidence the run already has. Without a count the general absence reason is unchanged.

changes.title: A kebab adjective is no longer extracted as a component subject
changes.description: Session 307's "role-protected admin console" produced the review subject "role-protected", so the model was told to read a component no path can match; qualifier suffixes (`-protected`, `-based`, `-driven`, `-ready`, …) are skipped and the qualified noun is named instead.

changes.title: Root-scoped absence claims ("No README at repo root") are no longer promoted to repository-wide
changes.description: claims by the word "repo" inside "repo root". A complete root listing covers them; the repository-wide form still requires coverage that can establish it, so an unrelated mention of the root does not weaken a real global claim.

changes.title: `glob` expands `{ts,tsx}` alternation instead of treating the pattern as a literal
changes.description: A shell-style pattern previously matched nothing and reported "no files matched", which reads as an empty tree and sends the model into a retry loop; expansion is bounded and nested groups are supported.

changes.title: A survey answer that bounds its negatives to what it inspected is no longer reviewed as a
changes.description: repository-wide absence claim. "No tests detected in inspected scope (test inventory not queried)" completes; "the project has no tests" still needs coverage. The bounded-scope and non-observation forms are recognised as claims, contractions are normalised, and the repository-wide veto now outranks the literal marker list instead of being bypassed by it.

changes.title: `structure` overview no longer reports declaration totals it never observed
changes.description: Navigation counts (`symbols`, `references`, `calls`, `tests`) render `0 (source not parsed)` before parsing and `unobservable (no adapter)` when no adapter can parse the inventoried sources; `test_files` stays a number because it is classified from paths at inventory time. Previously a Go-only build over a TypeScript project printed `tests: 0 (test_files: 0)`, which an answer read as "the project has no tests" — an absence the inventory cannot establish, and a `needs_review` on an otherwise grounded survey.

changes.title: A structural snapshot no longer reports `PARTIAL` when no adapter in this build can parse its
changes.description: sources. The verdict is `UNSUPPORTED` with the decisive limitation (`no adapter for .ts, .tsx; 0 of 5 source files parsed`), and the header names the compiled `adapters:` so a symbol-free result is attributable to the code or to the build variant.

changes.title: A truncated `structure` result now names the slice it cut and the total it refers to (`result:
changes.description: TRUNCATED (files 10 of 14)`), and the overview exposes the same counts as `bounds`. Previously a 14-file repository reported `result: TRUNCATED` with `result_reason: file_limit` while the rendered text showed the complete file count and no file list, so the model could not tell what was cut and issued a redundant inventory query.

changes.title: `structure` overview applies its entrypoint bound to the merged entrypoint list, reports
changes.description: `entrypoints:` from that list instead of the symbol-only snapshot count, and no longer prints a slice as cut when a view displayed more entries than the snapshot counted.

changes.title: A semantic migration target is no longer read as a file path
changes.description: `Target` now carries explicit `technology`, `repository`, `command`, and `resource` kinds alongside `path`/`symbol`/`package`, and `IntentContract.MutationScope` states whether a persistent change is bounded to named files/directories or the whole workspace. "Convert this project to Next.js" therefore produces a technology objective with workspace scope instead of a target named `Next.js`; completion no longer requires a changed path to contain the technology name.

changes.title: Shell mutations now carry provenance
changes.description: The recovery edit journal exposes the workspace diff it already captured, and completion classifies each change as `EXPECTED`, `UNEXPECTED`, `UNATTRIBUTED`, or `OUTSIDE_WORKSPACE` from the run's journal, a tool's own `AffectedPaths`, or the security scope. A shell mutation whose command text names no paths is attributed to the current task instead of `<unattributed>`; with no journal evidence it still requires review. A deterministically named persistent write outside the workspace (and outside the temporary execution area) is refused before the process starts.

changes.title: An approved widening transition now runs the objective it approved
changes.description: The handoff records the approving request's objective (`Handoff.ApprovedObjective`), the turn gate attaches only that objective, and `Controller.Begin` re-scopes the task's completion contract to it while keeping identity, carried context, and observed evidence. Previously ASK → BUILD ran the task's previous informational contract, so the BUILD turn was shaped as a read-only investigation: no write or command capability was offered, the model reported that it could not edit, and an execution request came back as a manual implementation plan.

changes.title: A capability the task surface withholds is now classified as `tool_capability_unavailable` instead
changes.description: of an unclassified candidate rejection, so a withheld proposal is diagnosable without parsing prose.

changes.title: A reasoning-only assistant turn is no longer replayed as conversation content
changes.description: The retried empty answer stayed in the run's turns, and every host rebuilt its next request from them; the resulting assistant message had no sendable block and providers rejected it (`messages[13].content`, a text part with no `text`). `agent.ConversationMessages` is now the single projection for live history, persistence, and session replay, and `session.Replay` skips a stored display-only assistant row instead of failing the resume.

changes.title: The canonical message contract is enforced before any transport serializes a request
changes.description: (`ai.ValidateMessages` at `Registry.StreamFn` and in the agent loop, with per-message provenance). An empty text part, an assistant turn with only reasoning, or a tool call without id/name is reported as `agent.ErrInvalidProviderContext` with the message index, role, provenance, and issue kind, instead of reaching a provider as `{"type":"text"}`. Serializers no longer fabricate empty text parts: an empty tool result is the empty string, and a call-only assistant turn omits content.

changes.title: `/commit` no longer fails with "the COMMIT model ran out of output budget" for a
changes.description: reasoning-by-default model whose role effort is `off`. Omitting the effort selected the provider default and spent the whole completion on hidden reasoning; the role now sends the lowest published effort when the model cannot be disabled, and the single truncation retry raises the completion budget instead of repeating the same cap.

changes.title: A reused or refused tool outcome now publishes its start/finish pair in its own turn
changes.description: A stale read that had actually run earlier can no longer be replayed after the final answer by the host's post-run fallback, which now publishes per completed turn.

changes.title: A substantive answer that shares one assistant message with a batch that cannot add
changes.description: evidence—every call is withheld by the task stage or repeats an observation already current in the run—is now the agent loop's terminal transition. Those continuation calls are dropped before dispatch, so a finished answer is no longer followed by refusal or reuse cards. A new offered capability keeps the normal path because the text may be narration before real work; a message that only announces an action keeps the bounded recovery, and policy-sensitive proposals remain visible.

changes.title: An invalid tool invocation no longer poisons capability health or blocks a recoverable task
changes.description: Argument, selector, unknown-tool, unsupported-operation, authority, budget, and stale-evidence failures are request-level: the identical request is refused once with schema-grounded correction, a corrected request remains eligible, and only genuine capability failures enter provider health. A failed structural provider is reconciled against independent authorized providers (README, manifests, listings, source reads), a successful overview survives a later targeted failure, and completion only excuses a pending provider failure when the evidence contract is actually satisfied. This closes the session-224 failure mode where `structure backend` was reported as a `remote_tool_error` and blocked the project analysis.

changes.title: A project-analysis request that opens with an ambiguous read verb and adds a later explicit read
changes.description: clause (`check this project and analyze what this project is about?`) now carries a strong READ signal and reaches the ASK authority boundary instead of silently staying in BUILD.

changes.title: An investigative opener followed by an explanatory clause (`investigate this project and analyze
changes.description: what this project is about?`) now remains a strong INVESTIGATE request. The explanatory clause describes the investigation's deliverable instead of contesting it into an ambiguous READ, so an automatic BUILD session hands the turn to FUZZ before the model runs. `trace` and `explore`, and causal/relational inquiry such as `find why`, `find where`, and `analyze how`, are investigation signals; `analyze what` and other pure explanations remain READ. A leading investigation followed by a change ("investigate and fix the checkout failure") starts in FUZZ and hands off to BUILD after evidence exists.

changes.title: An automatic one-shot handoff now updates the session's persisted workspace and model snapshot
changes.description: A turn that ran under FUZZ is no longer listed or resumed as BUILD because only the in-memory session recorded the move.

changes.title: A truncated metadata overview's `tests
changes.description: 0` is no longer treated as proof that no tests exist. Only a complete, unscoped structural test inventory (or the narrow complete Go scan) can support a test-file absence claim, and the state block reports a partial inventory as `absence unproven`.

changes.title: A configuration-derived runtime claim is no longer promoted by a Makefile/Compose/README observation
changes.description: The runtime state block reports `implementation=NOT_OBSERVED` and `runtime=NOT_OBSERVED`, and the completion audit still rejects an active behavior claim without source or runtime evidence.

changes.title: An implementation-status claim ("fully implemented", "stubs (health checks only)", "scaffolded")
changes.description: can no longer be supported by a README, manifest, Compose file, directory listing, or structural inventory. The answer audit requires a source observation for each named component and names the missing component in the review reason; reading one component does not support a claim about another.

changes.title: A behavior claim that names a port must be supported by a source observation containing that same
changes.description: port or by a live runtime address on that port. Reading one service's listener no longer supports a claim about a different service's port.

changes.title: Structural inventory no longer loses a nested repository to the enclosing repository's `.gitignore`
changes.description: A root rule such as `backend/` no longer reports `go: 0` when `backend/` is a nested Go project; the boundary is included, disclosed, and its tests remain discoverable.

changes.title: A malformed call can no longer downgrade a proof the runtime already holds
changes.description: A schema violation never executed, so it is neither work nor an observation about the project: completion ignores it for pending failures and outstanding work, and a late malformed continuation after a successful runtime verification still reports the objective as proven.

changes.title: A complete evidence lifecycle is an answer-only surface
changes.description: The projection now marks `StageComplete` as answer-eligible in addition to withdrawing every tool, so a continuation call cannot be dispatched once the objective's evidence is complete even if a future narrowing leaves a capability behind.

changes.title: `verify` accepts the equivalent argument shapes models routinely emit instead of spending a turn on
changes.description: a harness contract error: a single literal for `checks[].contains` is the same assertion as a one-element list, and a service `cwd` may be an absolute path inside the workspace (an absolute path outside it is still refused as an escape).

changes.title: The recap attributes the outcome to the observation that proved it
changes.description: A live runtime is narrated as "Ran <service> and verified <url> answered", not as the environment probes that ran while the model oriented itself; a sentence announcing an observation still to come is no longer quoted as a finding.

changes.title: Running the project is no longer reported `PROVEN` by a command that merely finished
changes.description: `run this project`, `run it`, `run the app`, `start the dev server`, and package-manager `start`/`dev` scripts are runtime execution contracts: completion requires a live runtime observation (service reached readiness, a check passed while it was alive, and it stayed up). An environment probe such as `node -v && npm -v` leaves the task active with the runtime gap named instead of closing the tool surface, and an older checkpoint whose command-only proof supported a false `PROVEN` now reports `COMPLETED_UNPROVEN`.

changes.title: `run it` after a runtime or execution task is an execution follow-up, not a verification
changes.description: It continues an open task instead of aborting with an objective conflict, and a finished task no longer answers “already proven” instead of running again. `is it running?` remains a verification question.

changes.title: Service requests now route to execution instead of ASK
changes.description: `use npx live-server test this project`, `serve this project and verify it`, and `start the development server and check the page` are execution contracts, and a bare “test this project” accepts behavioural HTTP/browser evidence rather than requiring a code-test check.

changes.title: Execution protocol failures are classified at the stage they occurred
changes.description: `NO_MODEL_OUTPUT`, `EXECUTION_INTENT_WITHOUT_TOOL`, and `TOOL_NORMALIZATION_FAILED`. Each gets at most one bounded recovery request; prose is never executed, malformed syntax is never dispatched, and a second failure ends in a review verdict rather than a retry loop.

changes.title: Stale checkpoints no longer present a contradictory runtime state
changes.description: A non-terminal task drops an impossible completion proof, and an older informational projection of an explicit service-execution objective is re-derived from the same user text before the resumed turn is routed.

changes.title: Background jobs are no longer orphaned
changes.description: session shutdown terminates every running job's process group, while normal turns still leave detached jobs available to `wait`.
